eyebrow: Python for Data Engineers · Chapter 5, Lesson 26
subtitle: Direct database connectivity with pyodbc.

code:
pip install pyodbc

# pyodbc talks to SQL Server over ODBC -- the Open
# Database Connectivity standard. It needs an ODBC
# driver installed on your machine (e.g. "ODBC Driver
# 18 for SQL Server"), usually installed alongside
# SQL Server or SSMS.
caption: pyodbc is the standard way to talk to SQL Server from Python.

code:
import pyodbc

conn = pyodbc.connect(
    "DRIVER={ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server};"
    "SERVER=localhost;"
    "DATABASE=AdventureWorks2012;"
    "Trusted_Connection=yes;"
)
caption: DRIVER, SERVER, DATABASE, and Trusted_Connection -- four pieces, semicolon-separated.

code:
cursor = conn.cursor()
cursor.execute("SELECT @@VERSION;")
row = cursor.fetchone()
print(row[0])

conn.close()
caption: cursor.execute() runs the SQL; fetchone() pulls back a single row as a tuple.
